s.q: Tangent and normal at $(x_1,y_1)$
Lengths of tangent, normal, subtangent, subnormal
Angle between two curves
Rate of change
s.n: Approximation: $\Delta y\approx f'(x)\Delta x$; relative error $\frac{\Delta y}y$.

s.q: Tangent parallel / perpendicular to axes
Tangent from an external point to a curve
s.f: y_0-f(a)=f'(a)(x_0-a)\ \text{solve for the point of contact } a

s.q: Common tangent to two curves
Curves touching each other
Approximation using differentials
s.f: f(a+h)\approx f(a)+hf'(a);\qquad\text{percentage error in } y=x^n:\ n\times(\text{percentage error in } x)

s.q: Increasing and decreasing
s.n: $f'\ge0$ with equality only at isolated points still gives strictly increasing.

s.q: Using monotonicity for inequalities
Monotonic on an interval — conditions on a parameter
s.f: f'(x)\ge0\ \forall x\ \text{(with equality at isolated points)}\Rightarrow\text{use } D\le0 \text{ or min value}\ge0

s.q: Monotonicity of composite functions
Comparing numbers via monotonic functions
Standard inequalities from monotonicity
First derivative test
Second derivative test
s.n: If $f''(c)=0$: check the first non-zero higher derivative; odd order → no extremum (point of inflection), even order → extremum.

s.q: Absolute extrema on $[a,b]$
s.f: \text{compare } f\ \text{at critical points and at } a,\ b

s.q: Point of inflection
s.f: f''(x)\ \text{changes sign};\ \ \text{concave up if } f''>0,\ \text{down if } f''<0

s.q: Critical points
Global extremum of a cubic on $\mathbb R$
s.f: \text{none (cubic is unbounded)};\ \text{local max/min exist iff } f'=0\ \text{has distinct roots}

s.q: Maximum of product with constraint using derivative
s.f: \text{express in one variable, differentiate, check sign change}

s.q: Distance from a point to a curve minimised
Concavity and point of inflection condition (cubic)
Standard optimisation results
s.f: \text{fixed perimeter}\Rightarrow\text{square has max area};\quad\text{fixed area}\Rightarrow\text{square has min perimeter}
s.n: Max rectangle in a circle of radius $r$: square, area $2r^2$. Max rectangle in an ellipse: $2ab$.

s.q: Cylinder and cone results
s.f: \text{open cylinder, fixed volume, min surface}: h=r;\quad\text{closed cylinder}: h=2r
s.n: Cone of max volume in a sphere of radius $R$: $h=\frac{4R}3$. Cylinder of max volume in a sphere: $h=\frac{2R}{\sqrt3}$. Cone with fixed slant height, max volume: $\tan\theta=\sqrt2$ (semi-vertical angle).

s.q: Shortest distance from a point to a curve
Number of roots via graph
s.f: f(x)=k\ \text{has as many roots as intersections of } y=f(x) \text{ and } y=k
s.n: Use local max/min values: between them → 3 roots for a cubic.

s.q: Cubic with three real roots
s.f: x^3+px+q=0\ \text{has three distinct real roots iff } 4p^3+27q^2<0

s.q: Global inequality from convexity
Rectangle of max area inscribed in a semicircle
Window / Norman window
s.f: \text{rectangle + semicircle, perimeter } P:\ \text{max area when width}=\frac{2P}{\pi+4}

s.q: Box from a square sheet by cutting squares
Cone inscribed in a cone / cylinder in a cone
s.f: \text{max volume cylinder in cone of height } h:\ \text{height }\frac h3

s.q: Triangle of max area with fixed perimeter / in a circle
Maximum of $f(x)=\frac{x}{\ln x}$ type — use derivative sign table
s.f: \text{for products/quotients, take log first, then differentiate}

s.q: Number of real roots of $f(x)=0$ using extrema
s.f: \text{if } f(\text{local max})\cdot f(\text{local min})<0\ \text{then three real roots (cubic)}

s.q: Rolle-type existence results
s.f: f(a)=f(b)=0\Rightarrow f'(c)+\lambda f(c)=0\ \text{for some } c\ (\text{apply Rolle to } e^{\lambda x}f)

s: If this type comes, solve like this

s.q: If it asks where $f$ is increasing or decreasing (sign of $f'$)
s.r: "$(2,3)$ is the largest interval where $2\ln(x-2)-x^2+ax+1$ increases", "$(3x-7)x^{2/3}$ is increasing for…", "$x^x$ increases on…", "$xe^{x(1-x)}$", "$3\ln|\frac{x-1}{x+1}|-\frac2{x-1}$".
s.s: Write the domain. || Differentiate and factor $f'(x)$ completely (including denominators and points where $f'$ does not exist). || Mark zeros and undefined points on a number line; find the sign in each interval (wavy curve). || Read the intervals; an endpoint of a "largest interval" is a zero of $f'$, which fixes a parameter.

s.q: If the function is piecewise, composite or built from a functional equation, and its monotonic intervals are asked
s.r: "$f$ given in three pieces; set where it increases", "$5f(x)+4f(\frac1x)=x^2-2$, $y=9x^2f(x)$", "$x\cos^{-1}(-\sin|x|)$", "$h=f\circ g$ with $f=e^x-x$, $g=x^2-x$", "$e^{x^3-3x+1}$ one-one onto".
s.s: Find the explicit formula (solve the functional equation, or write each piece). || Differentiate each piece and study the sign on its own interval; check the joining points. || For composites, the sign of $f'(g(x))g'(x)$ is the product of two signs. || For one-one onto, the function must be monotonic on the domain; its range gives $(a,b]$.
s.e: $h'(x)=(e^{x^2-x}-1)(2x-1)$: positive when both factors have the same sign ⇒ $x\in[0,\frac12]\cup[1,\infty)$.

s.q: If the function has trig terms or $\frac1x\ln(1+x)$ and its monotonic nature is asked
s.s: Differentiate and factor; for trig, take out $\cos x$ or $\sin x$ and factor the polynomial in the other. || Determine the sign on the interval. || For $\frac{\ln(1+x)}x$, consider the numerator of $f'$: $\frac{x}{1+x}-\ln(1+x)<0$, so $f$ decreases.
s.e: $f'=12\sin x\cos x(\sin^2x+\frac52\sin x+1)=12\sin x\cos x(\sin x+2)(\sin x+\frac12)$.

s.q: If the number of real roots of an equation is asked
s.f: \text{cubic } f \text{ has 3 real roots}\iff f(x_{\max})\cdot f(x_{\min})<0
s.s: Substitute $t=e^x>0$ if exponentials appear. || Find the critical points and the values of $f$ there. || Count sign changes between consecutive critical points and towards $\pm\infty$. || For parameters: write $a=g(x)$ and count intersections of the horizontal line $y=a$ with $y=g(x)$.
s.e: $5x^3-15x$ has local max $10$ at $x=-1$, min $-10$ at $x=1$; three roots iff $a\in(-10,10)$; $\beta-2\alpha=30$.

s.q: If it is a rate-of-change problem (melting coat, filling cone, expanding cube or balloon)
s.r: "Ice of uniform thickness melts at $50\text{ cm}^3/\text{min}$", "water into a cone at $1\text{ cm}^3/\text{s}$", "surface area of a cube increasing at $3.6$", "balloon's surface area increases at a constant rate".
s.s: Write the quantity (volume/area) in terms of one variable only (use similar triangles for cones). || Differentiate with respect to $t$ by the chain rule. || Substitute the given rate and the instant's value. || Solve for the unknown rate.

s.q: If $g(x)=f(\phi(x))+\ldots$ with $f''>0$ and it asks where $g$ increases or decreases
s.r: "$g(x)=3f(\frac x3)+f(3-x)$, $f''>0$ on $(0,3)$", "$g(x)=f(\tan^2x-2\tan x+4a)$", "for which $a$ is $f(g(x))$ increasing".
s.s: Differentiate $g$; the result compares $f'$ at two arguments. || Since $f'$ is increasing, $f'(u)-f'(v)$ has the sign of $u-v$. || Solve the simple inequality between the arguments.

s.q: If an inverse function's value and derivative are needed ($\frac{g(c)}{g'(c)}$)
s.s: Solve $f(x)=c$ for $x$ (guess small integers). || That $x$ is $g(c)$. || $g'(c)=\frac1{f'(x)}$.

s.q: If a parameter must make $f$ increasing for all $x$
s.r: "Largest $\lambda$ for which $4\lambda x^3-36\lambda x^2+36x+48$ is increasing on $\mathbb R$".
s.s: Differentiate: $f'$ is a quadratic. || Demand $f'\ge0$ for all $x$: leading coefficient $>0$ and $D\le0$. || Solve for the parameter, take the extreme value, and evaluate.

s.q: If Rolle's theorem, MVT or convexity is used to prove or count something
s.r: "$f(0)=3$, $f(1)=5$, line $y=2x+3$ meets the graph at only two points", "$f(2)=f(4)=0$: there exist $x_1,x_2$ with $f'(x_1)=-1$…", "$fm^2-2f'm+f''=0$ has equal roots", "$\sin x+3x-\frac2\pi(x^2+x)$".
s.s: Identify an interval where the hypotheses hold. || Apply MVT/Rolle to get points where $f'$ takes given values. || Apply again to $f'$ to get information on $f''$. || Equal roots in $m$ means $(f')^2=ff''$, i.e. $\left(\frac{f'}f\right)'=0$: $f=Ae^{kx}$.

s.q: If an inequality or a comparison of function values is asked via monotonicity
s.r: "$\frac x{\sqrt{a^2+x^2}}-\frac{d-x}{\sqrt{b^2+(d-x)^2}}$ is increasing?", "$|\ln x|-|x-1|$: which statements are true", "$(2-\sin\frac1x)|x|$", "$\lim\frac{f(5x)}{f(x)}$ with $f$ increasing and $\frac{f(7x)}{f(x)}\to1$".
s.s: Differentiate and show $f'>0$ (or study pieces separately for moduli). || Use monotonicity to order values. || For limit comparisons, trap $\frac{f(5x)}{f(x)}$ between $1$ and $\frac{f(7x)}{f(x)}$.

s.q: If critical points of a polynomial (or log/power function) are given and its coefficients or extreme values are asked
s.r: "$x=-1$, $x=2$ critical points of $x^3+ax^2+b\ln|x|+1$", "degree-5 polynomial with critical points $\pm1$ and $\lim(2+\frac{f(x)}{x^3})=4$", "touches the x-axis at $(-2,0)$", "$(3x^2+ax-2-a)e^x$ with critical point $x=1$".
s.f: f'(c)=0\ \text{at each critical point};\ \ f'\ \text{has the factors } (x-c_i)
s.s: Write $f'(x)$ with unknown coefficients and set $f'(c_i)=0$ (or write $f'=k\prod(x-c_i)$ for polynomials). || Use the extra condition (a value, a limit, touching an axis) to fix the remaining constants. || Integrate $f'$ if needed. || Then compute max/min values.
s.e: Degree 4 with critical points $-1,0,1$: $f'=kx(x^2-1)$, so $f=\frac k4x^4-\frac k2x^2+c$; $f(x)=f(0)$ ⇒ $x^2=0,2$, sum of squares $4$.

s.q: If the location of the local max/min is given and a parameter is found
s.r: "$2x^3-9ax^2+12a^2x+1$ has a local max at $\alpha$ and min at $\alpha^2$", "$f$ and $g$ have a common extreme point", "maximum for some $x<0$ and minimum for some $x>0$".
s.s: Factor $f'$ to find the critical points in terms of the parameter. || Decide which is max and which is min (sign of $f''$ or leading coefficient). || Impose the condition (e.g. $\alpha^2=2a$, or roots of opposite sign: product of roots $<0$).

s.q: If the absolute maximum/minimum on a closed interval is asked
s.r: "$|2x^2+3x-2|+\sin x\cos x$ on $[0,1]$", "piecewise function: sum of local minimum values", "$|5x-7|+[x^2+2x]$ on $[\frac54,2]$", "$\tan^{-1}(\sin x-\cos x)$ on $[0,\pi]$", "$3\sqrt{x-2}+\sqrt{4-x}$".
s.f: \text{candidates: endpoints, zeros of } f',\ \text{points where } f' \text{ fails to exist}
s.s: List the candidate points: endpoints, critical points, corners (modulus zero), jumps ($[\ ]$ changes). || Evaluate $f$ at each. || Largest is the absolute max, smallest the absolute min. || For $a\sqrt{x-p}+b\sqrt{q-x}$: max by Cauchy–Schwarz, min at an endpoint.

s.q: If it is a geometric optimisation (rectangle under a curve, wire cut into shapes, solids with fixed area)
s.r: "Largest rectangle with $A,B$ on the x-axis and $C,D$ on $y=x^2-1$", "20 m wire into a square and a circle", "cuboid $2x,4x,5x$ and hemisphere with fixed total area", "largest triangle in a circle".
s.f: \text{write the quantity in one variable, set } \frac{d}{dx}=0
s.s: Choose one variable and express everything with it (use the constraint). || Write the quantity to optimise. || Differentiate, set to zero, check it is a max/min. || Useful facts: largest triangle in a circle is equilateral; wire into square+circle has minimum area when the side equals the diameter.

s.q: If the closest point to a line, minimum triangle area, or min/max of a distance-type expression is asked
s.r: "Point of $y=x^2+4$ closest to $y=4x-1$", "line through $(3,5)$; minimum area of $OAB$", "max and min of $(\sqrt{8x-x^2-12}-4)^2+(x-7)^2$".
s.f: \text{closest point: tangent} \parallel \text{line};\ \ \text{min area through }(h,k):\ 2hk;\ \ \text{distance}^2 \text{ form}\Rightarrow\text{point on a circle}
s.s: For closest point, set $\frac{dy}{dx}$ equal to the line's slope. || For triangles with the axes through $(h,k)$, AM–GM on $\frac ha+\frac kb=1$ gives $ab\ge4hk$. || Recognise $(\sqrt{\ldots}-4)^2+(x-7)^2$ as the squared distance from a point on a semicircle to $(7,4)$.

s.q: If the max/min of a trig expression is asked
s.r: "$\max16\sin\frac x2\cos^3\frac x2$ on $[0,\pi]$", "$(1-\cos^2x)(\lambda+\sin x)$ has exactly one max and one min", "least $\alpha$ for $\frac4{\sin x}+\frac1{1-\sin x}=\alpha$".
s.s: Substitute $t=\sin x$ (or the half angle) to get a function on an interval. || Differentiate, or use Cauchy/AM–GM. || For "exactly one max and one min", the derivative must have exactly two sign changes in the interval.

s.q: If the function is $\left(\frac ax\right)^{x^2}$ or $x^{1/x}$ type
s.r: "Local maximum value of $\left(\frac2x\right)^{x^2}$".
s.s: Take logs. || Differentiate and set to zero: $2x\ln\frac ax-x=0\Rightarrow x=\frac a{\sqrt e}$. || Substitute back.

s.q: If the function is an integral with variable limits (count its maxima/minima)
s.r: "$f(x)=\int_0^{x^2}\frac{t^2-5t+4}{2+e^t}dt$; numbers of local max and min".
s.s: Differentiate using the Leibniz rule. || Factor: here $2x(x^2-1)(x^2-4)$. || Make a sign chart; $-\to+$ is a minimum, $+\to-$ a maximum.

s.q: If the number or nature of critical points is asked for modulus, power or composite functions
s.f: (x-a)^n:\ n \text{ even}\Rightarrow\text{extremum at } a;\ n \text{ odd}\Rightarrow\text{no extremum (inflection)}
s.s: Find zeros of $f'$ and points where $f'$ does not exist (corners, cusps). || Check sign changes of $f'$ around each. || For powers $(x-a)^n$: even $n$ gives an extremum, odd $n$ gives none. || For $3^{g(x)}$, extrema of $f$ are those of $g$.

s.q: If the parameter must be chosen so that there are no critical points, or the minimum lies in a region
s.r: "$(p^2-6p+8)(\sin^22x-\cos^22x)+2(2-p)x+7$ has no critical point", "local min of $1+x(\lambda^2-x^2)$ satisfies an inequality", "$x\sqrt{kx-x^2}$ increasing on $[0,3]$".
s.f: \text{no critical point}\iff f'(x)\ne0\ \forall x\iff |\text{oscillating part}|<|\text{constant part}|
s.s: Write $f'$ as (constant) + (bounded trig part). || No critical point: the trig part can never cancel the constant: $|A|\cdot\max|\ldots|<|B|$. || For location conditions, find the critical point in terms of the parameter and substitute into the inequality.

s.q: Mixed max–min (maximum slope, functional equations, matrices with $x$, best term of an AP)
s.r: "Maximum slope of $y=\frac12x^4-5x^3+18x^2-19x$", "$f(\frac{x+y}3)=\frac{f(x)+f(y)}3$", "$f(x)=\det(A)$ with $x$ entries", "$a_1a_4a_5$ greatest in an AP with $a_6=2$", "$f''=g''+6x$".
s.s: Translate the problem into a single-variable function. || For the maximum slope, maximise $y'$: set $y''=0$. || For AP products, write each term in $d$ and maximise. || For $f''=g''+6x$, integrate twice with the given values.
